title: Synthesis, decomposition and displacement
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:22Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The new point teaches all three reaction types together, but no single bank point covers that: the synthesis and decomposition card lacks displacement, and the displacement card covers only that one type.

draft.title: Synthesis, decomposition and displacement
card: two or more substances join to make one product. For example, iron + sulfur → iron sulfide.
one substance breaks into two or more simpler substances. For example, water → hydrogen + oxygen.
a more reactive element takes the place of a less reactive element in a compound. For example, magnesium + copper sulfate → magnesium sulfate + copper.
To classify a reaction, look at how many substances are on each side of the arrow and whether an element swaps places in a compound.
draft.remember: Synthesis joins, decomposition splits, displacement swaps a less reactive element for a more reactive one.

a.q: Calcium carbonate is heated and forms calcium oxide and carbon dioxide. What type of reaction is this?
a.why: One substance, calcium carbonate, breaks into two simpler substances, so it is decomposition. It is not synthesis, which would have several substances joining into one.
a.clue: Count the substances before and after the arrow.

b.q: Zinc metal is placed in copper sulfate solution. Zinc is more reactive than copper. Zinc sulfate and copper form. What type of reaction is this?
opts: Displacement, as zinc takes copper's place in the compound
Synthesis, as zinc and copper sulfate join together
Decomposition, as copper sulfate breaks into two products
Displacement, as copper takes zinc's place in the compound
b.why: The more reactive zinc takes the place of copper in the compound, leaving copper metal. Two substances react and two form, so it is not synthesis or decomposition. The last option reverses which element is more reactive.
b.clue: Which element is more reactive, and which one ends up alone?

b.best: Displacement, as zinc takes copper's place in the compound
